newsitem.title: USA: U.S. museum discovers a treasure in its collection.
newsitem.headline: U.S. museum discovers a treasure in its collection.

text.p: The Art Institute of Chicago said on Thursday it had found a major work by an 18th century French master in its own collection.
The painting, Fete Champetre, has been authenticated as the work of Antoine Watteau, who it described as the greatest French painter and draftsman of his time.
The work was given to the museum in 1954 and attributed at the time to an anonymous "follower of Jean Batiste Pater." Pater was a pupil of Watteau.

Two years ago researchers began to investigate the work which was badly clouded with varnish. The institute said a scientific examination and X-ray analysis had proven it to be a Watteau, one that due to the scarcity of his work and its market value the museum would be unable to afford to buy today.
